rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for acting foolishly or behaving stupidly.

example.english: Don't fool around during the meeting.
example.traditional: 你開會嗰陣唔好發傻呀。
example.jyutping: nei5 hoi1 wui2 go2 zan6 m4 hou2 faat3 so4 aa3

rows.note: Use this when the foolishness consists specifically of doing stupid or ill-judged things rather than merely behaving foolishly.

example.english: You fool around by borrowing from loan sharks to chase girls.
example.traditional: 為咗追女仔去借貴利，你真係做傻事喎。
example.jyutping: wai6 zo2 zeoi1 neoi5 zai2 heoi3 ze3 gwai3 lei6 nei5 zan1 hai6 zou6 so4 si6 wo3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for a person with poor judgment or little intelligence.

example.english: You're a fool to believe that.
example.jyutping: nei5 zan1 hai6 so2 zai2 gam2 dou1 seon3

rows.note: Use this as a slightly more playful or affectionate alternative when calling someone a fool.

example.jyutping: so2 gwaa1 m4 hou2 m4 hoi1 sam1 aa3

rows.note: Use this for someone who has been tricked or is easy to exploit, especially financially.

example.english: He got tricked out of so much money—what a fool.
example.traditional: 佢畀人呃咗咁多錢，真係水魚。
example.jyutping: keoi5 bei2 jan4 aak1 zo2 gam3 do1 cin2 zan1 hai6 seoi2 jyu4

rows.note: Use this for someone who is especially enthusiastic about a particular hobby or subject.

example.english: My friend is a photography fool.
example.traditional: 我個朋友係攝影發燒友。
example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 pang4 jau5 hai6 sip3 jing2 faat3 siu1 jau5
